correctness.rationale: The Lorentz-cone proof is correct. Rank below three leaves at most two independent real measurements and violates the sharp complex PR-ae lower bound. At rank three the kernel is one-dimensional. Along a kernel line through a future null point, the cone equation has the original root and one explicit second root. A positive determinant makes the second root lie on the past cone; a negative determinant makes it another future point except on a proper tangency set of directions; determinant zero gives a rank-one semidefinite kernel and collapses exactly one complex signal line to the zero measurement. These cases give respectively full PR, PR-ae but not PR, and generic two-to-one failure.

originality.rationale: Originality passes for the complete trichotomy. Huang--Rong--Wang--Xu prove the sharp three-measurement lower bound and existence of three-measurement PR-ae systems in complex dimension two. Wang--Xu's general kernel criterion already implies the positive-determinant full-PR branch. The inspected general results do not state that every rank-three triple with a rank-one semidefinite kernel is PR-ae but not PR, nor that every indefinite kernel gives generic two-point fibers. Those boundary and negative-determinant branches are the new content of the final claim.

value.rationale: Three measurements are the exact minimum for complex almost-everywhere generalized phase retrieval in dimension two. Classifying every triple at that boundary, including the semidefinite exceptional line and the generic multiplicity in the indefinite regime, is a natural structural completion of the sharp measurement-count theorem.
